### Bible Pathways 02/09/05
Author: Bible Pathways
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-02-or-09-or-05-1309516.html
Passage: Leviticus 23:5-6
Points:
- Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread introduce Israel's sacred calendar, commemorating their deliverance from bondage.
- Consuming unleavened bread for seven days served as a reminder that the Israelites were set apart to the Lord.
- The absence of leaven typifies the sinless nature of Christ, the true Bread of God.
- Believers are called to purge the old yeast of wickedness and walk in sincerity and truth.

### Feast of Unleavened Bread: How a Hasty Escape Prepares Us to Wait for Christ
Author: J. Michael Thigpen
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/feast-unleavened-bread/
Passage: Leviticus 23:6-8
Points:
- The feast called Israel to eat unleavened bread for seven days and observe sacred assemblies without ordinary work.
- Eating bread made without leaven commemorated their urgent flight from Egypt and complete dependence on God.
- The annual celebration reinforced gratefulness for God's redemption and provision rather than discontentment.
- Christ fulfilled the Passover, and His people must now live ready and watchful for His return.
